1. Captioned appeal is filed against the impugned judgment and award dated 26.07.2019 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux) Panchmahals at Halol in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.2255 of 2017, whereby the learned Tribunal had partly allowed the claim petition and awarded a sum of Rs.1,20,824/- as a compensation along with the interest at the rate of 9% per annum from Balwantsinh Mahasukhbhai Chavda vs Vipulbhai Jasvantbhai Gohil on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117883427/

2. The succinct facts leading to file the captioned appeal are that on 04.11.2013, the Balwantsih Mahasukhbhai Chavda was going on his bicycle from his home towards Malav Ashram.

When he reached at the place of accident, in the meantime, opponent No.1- Vipulbhai Jasvantbhai Gohil came by driving the motorcycle bearing registration No.GJ-17-J-4350 in a rash and negligent manner at very excessive speed so as to endanger the human life and dashed with the applicant from behind.
As a result of the accident, the applicant sustained serious injuries.
Therefore, he filed claim petition seeking the compensation of Rs.4,00,000/-.
3. On being served, opponent No.2-Insurance Company had filed written statement at Exh-13 thereby denying all the averments made in the claim petition and prayed for rejection of the claim petition.
The opponent No.1 did not appear before the learned Tribunal.

4. Having considered the pleadings of the parties, the learned NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/442/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined Tribunal framed the following issues at Exh-11:-
"1. Whether it is proved that the claimant sustained injuries on account of rashness or negligence in driving on the part of the driver of the vehicle involved in the accident?
2. What amout, if any, the claimant is entitled to by way of compensation and from which of the opponents?
3.
What order?"

5. Having considered the pleadings, evidence and submissions made by the learned advocates for the respective parties, the learned Tribunal had partly allowed the claim petition and awarded a sum of Rs.1,20,824/- as a compensation along with the interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till realization.
The learned Tribunal had exonerated the respondent No.2-Insurance Company from satisfying the impugned judgment and award.

6. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award, the original claimants/appellants had challenged the impugned judgment and award on the ground of exoneration of the Insurance Company from satisfying the impugned judgment and award.

7. Heard learned advocates for the parties.
8.

Mr. K. K. Thakkar, learned advocate appearing on behalf of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/442/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined the original claimant, vehemently submitted that he is not challenging the impugned judgment and award on the ground of quantum.

But he is challenging the impugned judgment and award on the ground of exoneration of the Balwantsinh Mahasukhbhai Chavda vs Vipulbhai Jasvantbhai Gohil on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117883427/

In support of his contention, the learned advocate for the appellant has placed reliance upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court rendered in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Versus Swaran Singh & Ors.,
reported in (2004) 3 SCC 297, Mani Venkatesh S/O Palpandrum Versus M/s.

9 . On the other hand, Ms. Masumi Nanavati, learned advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No.2-Insurance NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/442/2020 JUDGMENT DATED:
05/03/2026 undefined Company, vehemently submitted that at the time of accident, the rider of the offending motorcycle was not holding the driving license to drive the said motorcycle.
Therefore, the learned Tribunal has rightly exonerated the Insurance Company.

She further submitted that the learned Tribunal or this Court cannot pass the order of pay and recover and the Hon'ble Supreme Court can pass the order of pay and recover in exercising power under Article 142 of the Constitution of India.

In support of her contention, learned advocate for the respondent No.2 has placed reliance upon the judgment rendered by Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in First Appeal No.1278 of 2010 titled as National Insurance Company Versus Laxmiben Ramanbhai Patel & 2 other(s), wherein the similar facts and circumstances, the Co- ordinate Bench has exonerated the Insurance Company from satisfying the impugned judgment and award.

sentences.text: Learned advocate for the respondent No.2- Insurance Company has also placed reliance upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court rendered in the case of Balu Krishna Chavan Versus The Reliance General Insurance Company Limited and Ors., reported in 2023 (1) TAC 130.

Having placed the reliance upon the aforesaid judgments, the learned advocate for the respondent No.2-Insurance Company submitted that the captioned appeal NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/442/2020 JUDGMENT DATED:
05/03/2026 undefined deserves to be rejected.
10. Having considered the submissions of the learned advocates for the parties and having gone through the record, it is not in dispute that the accident in question occurred on 04.11.2013.
The driving license came to be issued on 27.11.2015, therefore, at the time of accident, the respondent No.1 was not having the driving license to drive the motorcycle.
It is also not in dispute that at the time of accident, the offending motorcycle was duly insured by the respondent No.2-Insurance Company.
As to whether in the absence of driving license can the order of pay and recover be passed by the High Court.

The said issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court rendered in the case of Swaran Singh & Ors.(supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court in paragraph 108(x) observed as under:-
"108(x).

Where on adjudication of claim under the Act, the Tribunal arrives at a conclusion that the insurer has satisfactorily proved its defence in accordance with the provisions of Section 149(2) read with sub- section (7), as interpreted by this Court above, the Tribunal can direct that the insurer is liable to be reimbursed by the Balwantsinh Mahasukhbhai Chavda vs Vipulbhai Jasvantbhai Gohil on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117883427/
3 insured for the compensation and other amounts which it has been compelled to pay to the third party under the award of the Tribunal.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such determination of claim by the Tribunal will be enforceable and the money found due to the insurer from the insured will be recoverable on a certificate issued by the Tribunal to the Collector in the same manner under Section 174 of the Act as arrears of land revenue.

The certificate will be issued for the recovery as arrears of land revenue only if, as NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/442/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined required by sub-section (3) of Section 168 of the Act, The insurer fails to deposit the amount awarded in favour of the insurer within thirty days from the date of announcement of the award by the Tribunal."
11.

Further in case of Singh Ram(supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court where the insured did not hold the valid driving license at the time of accident, in para 8 observed as under:-
"8.
In the present case it is necessary to note, as observed by the Tribunal, that the owner did not depose in evidence and stayed away from the witness box.
He produced a licence which was found to be fake.
Another licence which he sought to produce had already expired before the accident and was not renewed within the prescribed period.
It was renewed well after two years had expired.

The appellant as owner had evidently failed to take reasonable care (proposition (vii) of Swaran Singh)
since he could not have been unmindful of facts which were within his knowledge."
12.

The issue as to whether the learned Tribunal can pass the order of pay and recover or the question falling for consideration before the Hon'ble Supreme Court as to whether the High Court was right in observing that only Supreme Court in exercise of its jurisdiction under Article 142 of the Constitution of India, can pass the order of pay and recover even in respect of third party claims.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mani Venkatesh(supra) observed as under:-
".....The issue raised in this appeal is squarely covered by the decision of this Court rendered in the case of Shamanna & Anr. Vs. The Divisional Manager, The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Ors., reported in (2018) 9 SCALE 456.

entities.text: Shamanna & Anr. Vs. The Divisional Manager, The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Ors., reported in (2018) 9 SCALE 456
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since the issue is covered by the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/442/2020 JUDGMENT DATED:
05/03/2026 undefined aforesaid judgment, the impugned judgment passed by the High Court is set aside and the appeal is allowed.

The first respondent/insurance company shall pay the compensation amount along with the accrued interest within a period of six weeks from today and the insurance company shall recover the same from the owner or the driver of the vehicle as held in Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Shri Nanjappan & Ors., reported in (2004) 13 SCC 224."

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Shri Nanjappan & Ors., reported in (2004) 13 SCC 224
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. Now, coming to the case on hand, there is no iota of doubt that the learned Tribunal or the High Court is vested with the power to issue the direction to the insurance company to first satisfy the award and then recover the same from the owner and the driver of the offending vehicle.

So far as the judgment relied upon by the learned counsel for the insurance company rendered in the case of Balwantsinh Mahasukhbhai Chavda vs Vipulbhai Jasvantbhai Gohil on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117883427/

sentences.text: Laxmiben Ramanbhai Patel(supra) delivered by the Coordinate Bench of this Court is not in consonance with the judgment delivered by the Full Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court rendered in the case of Swaran Singh (supra), Singh Ram(supra) and Division Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court rendered in the case of Mani Venkatesh(supra)
, therefore, the captioned appeal deserves to be allowed and accordingly, the impugned judgment is modified to the aforesaid extent.
The insurance company shall deposit the awarded amount along with interest within a period of six weeks from today.

After satisfying the award, the insurance company shall NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/442/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined be at liberty to recover the same from the respondent No.1- herein by way of filing the execution petition before the learned Tribunal concerned.
14. Upon depositing of said amount, the learned Tribunal shall disburse the said amount to the original claimant after deducting deficit of Court fee, if any, after due verification.
The amount, if any, lying/deposited with the registry of this Court, the same shall be transmitted to the learned Tribunal concerned forthwith.
No order as to costs.
15. Consequently, Civil Application also stands disposed of.
16. Record & Proceedings, if any, be sent back to the learned Tribunal concerned.
